letter.portfolio:
**Cartera recomendada — núcleo ordenado, con SCHAEFFLER como héroe**

1. **SCHAEFFLER — héroe.** Integración laboral post-adquisición en seis estados, para más de 5.000 empleados, con 35 procedimientos laborales activos; Eduardo Garduño lidera.
2. **Brose México.** Estrategia de negociación y litigio en una controversia de representatividad sindical; la fuente reporta prevención de paros y de escalamiento bajo el USMCA RRM; Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera.
3. **Volkswagen de México y Volkswagen Financial Services.** Cartera activa con exposición aproximada de MXN280 millones, combinada con documentación, reglamentos, disciplina y gobierno laboral; Eduardo Garduño lidera.
4. **Cinemex.** Plataforma nacional de aproximadamente 200 procedimientos activos, conciliaciones, restructuración y prevención para una fuerza laboral superior a 11.000 personas; Eduardo Garduño y Fernanda Priego figuran como líderes.
5. **GeNI de México.** Negociación colectiva ante riesgo inminente de huelga; la fuente reporta acuerdo renovado y continuidad productiva; Eduardo Garduño y Carlos Rivera figuran como líderes.
6. **Bonatti.** Estructuras laborales de ciclo completo para infraestructura energética, más de 20 controversias y prevención de una huelga reportada; Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera.
7. **Poliuretanos Summa Woodbridge.** Restructuración de aproximadamente ocho compañías, entidad de servicios especializados, sustituciones patronales y litigio de seguridad social pendiente; José Alberto Díaz Méndez figura como responsable del asunto y su cargo confirmado es Associate.
8. **Coats de México.** Transformación de plantilla en Puebla, Veracruz y Tlaxcala, con negociación colectiva y asuntos sindicales de exposición superior a MXN12,5 millones; Eduardo Garduño lidera.
9. **Recicla Ambiente.** Coordinación de estrategia laboral, negociación colectiva y relaciones sindicales para aproximadamente 700 empleados en seis localidades.
10. **Benteler.** Respuesta a controversia de representatividad sindical mediante litigio, estrategia colectiva y negociaciones con sindicatos competidores; Eduardo Garduño lidera.
11. **BADAK.** Defensa de reclamaciones por terminación; la fuente reporta reducción de una reclamación de aproximadamente MXN1,06 millones a MXN20.000, mientras continúan otros procedimientos; Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera.
12. **Nueva Empresa.** Amparo laboral que, según la fuente, obtuvo reconocimiento de la personería del apoderado y restituyó el derecho de defensa; Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera.
13. **Mextypsa.** Estructuración y desmovilización de plantilla para infraestructura, amparo y más de 20 controversias laborales en curso; Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera.
14. **Robert Bosch de México.** Documentación laboral, disciplina, asuntos sindicales, altas patronales y coordinación de seguridad social para una organización descrita con aproximadamente 17.000 empleados.
15. **Grupo Solana.** Reactivación de registro patronal para permitir una sustitución patronal sin interrupción operativa reportada; José Alberto Díaz Méndez figura como responsable y es Associate confirmado.
16. **SCOTCH.** Revisión REPSE, estructura societaria y laboral, y auditoría de más de 80 proveedores; José Alberto Díaz Méndez figura como responsable y es Associate confirmado.
17. **Empresa Tekia.** Litigación laboral heredada, negociaciones sobre sentencias adversas y amparo pendiente; Jaime Bustamante lidera.
18. **REGSA.** Documentación laboral, marco colectivo y procedimientos de representatividad sindical, sin resultado final declarado.
19. **Art Human.** Litigación, auditorías e inspecciones; la fuente reporta tres inspecciones de STPS e IMSS sin multas; Jaime Bustamante lidera.
20. **Grupo Radio Centro.** Investigación interna sensible; la fuente reporta prevención de litigio por aproximadamente MXN750.000; Jaime Bustamante lidera.

La cartera mantiene las distintas cantidades en su concepto correcto: valor del asunto, exposición litigiosa, valor de proyecto o litigio evitado no se intercambian ni se agregan.
letter.leadership:
**Estrategia individual.** La limitación común es clara: para los ocho abogados, la verificación de Chambers para Labour & Employment, México, arroja *not found* en la tabla examinada. Ese resultado no confirma ausencia de ranking en otras prácticas o ediciones y no constituye reconocimiento individual. Las categorías siguientes son objetivos de candidatura, no rangos establecidos.

**Eduardo Garduño — presentar como candidato individual principal; objetivo Band 5.** Es socio confirmado y concentra la evidencia individual más sólida. Lidera el héroe SCHAEFFLER; el mandato integrado de Volkswagen; la transformación y negociación colectiva de Coats; y la negociación de GeNI ante riesgo de huelga. Esta combinación acredita liderazgo personalmente atribuido en integración post-adquisición, relaciones colectivas, litigación de escala y gobierno laboral industrial. Su objetivo Band 5 procede del objetivo suministrado y debe presentarse sólo como candidatura. Próximo paso: obtener referencias que validen liderazgo, servicio y criterio comercial.

**Javier Atzin Vallejo — presentar como segundo candidato socio; categoría pendiente.** Es socio confirmado. Lidera Brose, Bonatti, Nueva Empresa y BADAK, articulando disputas colectivas, prevención de paros, proyectos energéticos, amparo y defensa de reclamaciones laborales. El objetivo fuente de “Associate to Watch” es incompatible con su condición confirmada de socio y ha sido correctamente sustituido por una categoría pendiente para socio; no hay base externa para proponer una banda. Próximo paso: definir un objetivo individual compatible con socio, sustentado en referencias y evidencia externa disponible.

**Jaime Bustamante — desarrollar como candidato socio; categoría pendiente.** Es socio confirmado y aparece como líder en Tekia, Art Human y Grupo Radio Centro. Los asuntos atribuidos muestran litigación compleja con amparo pendiente, auditorías e inspecciones laborales y de seguridad social, y una investigación interna sensible. La evidencia respalda una narrativa diferenciada de gestión de riesgo laboral, pero aún no define una categoría individual concreta. Próximo paso: obtener un objetivo de categoría y referencias que acrediten su liderazgo en esos mandatos.

**José Alberto Díaz Méndez — presentar como candidato Associate to Watch.** Su cargo confirmado es Associate. La fuente le atribuye responsabilidad en SCOTCH, Grupo Solana y PSW: REPSE y auditoría de más de 80 proveedores; sustitución patronal; y restructuración multi-entidad con componente de seguridad social. También aparece como miembro nombrado en Volkswagen, Coats, Benteler y Bosch. Esta concentración respalda una candidatura de Associate to Watch, siempre describiéndolo como Associate y responsable de los trabajos, nunca como socio. Próximo paso: obtener referencias y detalles de ejecución individual —por ejemplo, estrategia, autoridad, negociación o dirección técnica— para reforzar la candidatura.

**Erick Pérez — desarrollar, no presentar como candidato individual formal.** Es Associate confirmado y aparece como miembro de equipo en Cinemex, Volkswagen y Benteler. La evidencia apoya visibilidad de bench en litigación nacional, gobierno industrial y controversias sindicales, pero no especifica su función jurídica individual. Próximo paso: documentar al menos dos mandatos con responsabilidad concreta en litigio, inspección o negociación colectiva.

**Andrés Cabrera — no presentar este ciclo.** Es Associate confirmado, pero ningún asunto seleccionado le atribuye un mandato o rol individual. Su perfil de litigación laboral es coherente con la práctica, aunque una biografía no sustituye asuntos personalmente atribuidos. Próximo paso: reunir al menos dos mandatos relevantes con responsabilidad, actividad y resultado claramente descritos.

**Raymundo Carreño — no presentar este ciclo.** Es Associate confirmado y no tiene asuntos actuales atribuidos. Su experiencia histórica puede enriquecer una biografía, pero no acredita una candidatura actual. Próximo paso: incorporar trabajo reciente con rol específico en defensa, terminaciones o conciliación.

**Edgar Barreto — no presentar este ciclo.** Es Associate confirmado y tampoco dispone de asuntos atribuidos personalmente. El perfil refiere litigación laboral e IMSS, pero falta evidencia de ejecución individual. Próximo paso: desarrollar una cartera atribuida de litigación, seguridad social o investigaciones laborales.
letter.next_steps:
1. Confirmar una sola vez la ventana de investigación aplicable o que los mandatos seleccionados en curso tuvieron actividad relevante en ese periodo. La ausencia de fechas exactas no obliga a excluirlos.
2. Incorporar referencias de clientes, en particular para Eduardo Garduño, Javier Atzin Vallejo, Jaime Bustamante y José Alberto Díaz Méndez.

letter.evidence_gaps:
**Reservas y exclusiones comparativas.**

**Securitas de México** queda como reserva frente a **Cinemex**. Securitas demuestra más de 50 procedimientos y cobertura en Puebla, Ciudad de México, Torreón y Veracruz; Cinemex aporta una plataforma de aproximadamente 200 procedimientos, exposición superior a MXN60,5 millones, conciliaciones, restructuración y una contribución más clara a la visibilidad de Eduardo Garduño y Erick Pérez.

El asunto de **ex ejecutivo vinculado a Enerflex** queda como reserva frente a **Bonatti**. Su escala y complejidad de mediación son relevantes, pero la fuente identifica expresamente al empleado como cliente. Incluirlo en el núcleo desdibujaría la identidad employer-side. Bonatti conserva coherencia con esa identidad y contribuye directamente a la candidatura de Javier Atzin Vallejo.

**Ramsa Soluciones de Negocios en Bebidas** queda como reserva frente a **SCOTCH**. Ramsa fortalece la vertiente preventiva de Jaime Bustamante mediante auditorías, procedimientos, terminaciones y formación. SCOTCH es comparativamente más distintivo por su trabajo REPSE, la auditoría de más de 80 proveedores y su función central para demostrar la contribución individual de José Alberto Díaz Méndez.

**Corrugados y Empaques de Oriente** se excluye porque mezcla asesoría laboral y corporativa sin un problema laboral particularizado, escala, resultado o estado del asunto. **Sirushi/Shirushi** se excluye por ser asesoría laboral cotidiana menos diferenciada que el núcleo colectivo, restructuraciones y litigación; además, el nombre del cliente difiere entre el campo y la narrativa. **AUNDE** se excluye porque describe asesoría laboral y de seguridad social general sin cuestión jurídica, resultado, escala o estado concretos.
letter.executive_assessment:
**Veredicto ejecutivo — presentar para reconocimiento inicial.** La propuesta vigente sostiene una candidatura de primera inclusión en Labour & Employment, México, no una subida de bandas: la verificación disponible no encontró una coincidencia exacta de DeForest Abogados en la tabla examinada, lo que no acredita ausencia de ranking global ni una posición actual. Por ello, el objetivo secundario de “Move up multiple bands/tiers” queda correctamente descartado.

La principal fortaleza de la evidencia presentada es una práctica employer-side cohesionada que conecta relaciones colectivas, integración de plantillas, restructuraciones, litigación laboral, amparo, seguridad social y gobierno preventivo. La selección no se apoya únicamente en volumen: muestra intervenciones concretas en conflictos de representatividad sindical, negociación colectiva, transiciones de empleador, REPSE y plataformas de litigación para empleadores industriales, de infraestructura y de consumo.

El héroe debe seguir siendo **SCHAEFFLER**. Frente al mandato de Volkswagen, que aporta una exposición litigiosa mayor, SCHAEFFLER ofrece una demostración más precisa de transformación laboral: integración posterior a una adquisición, armonización de documentación individual y colectiva, reglamentos, comisiones mixtas y políticas de gobierno en seis estados para más de 5.000 empleados, junto con 35 procedimientos activos. Además, atribuye claramente el liderazgo a Eduardo Garduño.

La principal vulnerabilidad no es de práctica, sino de validación externa: no se suministran referencias de clientes ni evidencia comparativa de mercado, y la investigación de ranking no establece reconocimiento individual o institucional. Las afirmaciones de resultados se deben mantener como resultados reportados por las fuentes, sin transformarlas en validación independiente ni en previsiones de ranking.

strategy.thesis: The selected confidential and publishable evidence supports an employer-side Labour & Employment submission centred on collective bargaining and union-representation disputes, workforce integration and restructurings, labor litigation portfolios, constitutional remedies, and labor/social-security governance for industrial and geographically dispersed workforces. SCHAEFFLER is the hero because it most clearly combines post-acquisition integration across six states, a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees and linked active proceedings. The submission objective is first-time recognition; no firm or individual Chambers ranking is established by the supplied verification, which records no exact scoped match rather than confirming any unranked status.

The source states that work stoppages were prevented and escalation under the USMCA Rapid Response Labor Mechanism was avoided; these are source-reported results rather than independently verified findings.

development.c2:
DeForest respectfully seeks first-time recognition for its Labour & Employment practice in Mexico. The firm presents an employer-side practice that combines collective labour relations, workforce transformation, labour litigation, constitutional remedies, social-security work and preventive governance for industrial, infrastructure, technology, consumer-facing and regulated businesses.

Representative work includes a post-acquisition labour integration across six Mexican states for more than 5,000 employees, alongside 35 active labour proceedings; collective bargaining and union-representation mandates that have prevented work stoppages; a nationwide platform of approximately 200 active labour proceedings; and specialised-services restructurings involving employer substitutions, REPSE analysis and audits of more than 80 suppliers. The practice also handles employment investigations, labour and IMSS inspections, project-workforce structures and social-security litigation.

Eduardo Garduño, Javier Atzin Vallejo and Jaime Bustamante lead mandates across collective bargaining, industrial workforce governance, litigation and regulatory-risk management. José Alberto Díaz Méndez contributes to restructuring and specialised-services matters. Together, these mandates show a team supporting employers through the employment lifecycle, from preventive design and workforce integration to collective disputes and complex contentious matters.
development.b10:
DeForest’s Labour & Employment practice advises employers on workforce stability, collective labour relations, labour litigation, social security, compliance and workforce governance across Mexico. The team acts for industrial, infrastructure, technology, consumer-facing and regulated businesses where employment strategy is closely connected to operational continuity.

The practice combines contentious and non-contentious work. Its mandates include post-acquisition workforce integration across six Mexican states for more than 5,000 employees; collective bargaining and union-representativeness proceedings; nationwide litigation platforms involving hundreds of active matters; labour restructurings and employer-substitution processes; constitutional amparo proceedings; inspections and social-security matters; and specialised-services and REPSE projects.

The team’s work is particularly relevant to employers with manufacturing operations, geographically dispersed personnel, regulated workforces and sensitive union relationships. It designs employment documentation, collective bargaining frameworks, internal regulations, disciplinary procedures, compliance programmes and workforce-transition structures, while coordinating litigation and conciliation where disputes arise.

Eduardo Garduño leads employer-side mandates involving workforce integration, collective labour relations and labour-governance programmes. Javier Atzin Vallejo focuses on collective labour disputes, social security, infrastructure-related workforce structures and constitutional litigation. Jaime Bustamante advises on labour disputes, compliance, internal investigations and employment-risk management. José Alberto Díaz Méndez contributes to labour and social-security restructuring, REPSE analysis and administrative litigation, supported by a broader team working across contentious and advisory matters.

The practice’s identity is an integrated employer-side offering: collective relations, workforce transformation, litigation and preventive governance are managed as connected elements of operational continuity.

matters.text:
DeForest represents a confidential employer in two ongoing wrongful-termination proceedings that arose after a labour court refused to recognise the legal standing of the company’s attorney-in-fact and issued an adverse ruling without considering its defence. The recorded matter value is approximately USD171,494.21, distinct from the narrative’s approximately MXN3 million exposure figure.

The firm challenged the ruling through constitutional amparo proceedings. The Collegiate Court granted constitutional relief, ordered recognition of the attorney’s legal standing and restored the employer’s right to present its defence. Javier Atzin Vallejo leads, supported by Yrelia Barrón.
decisive_source_quotes: DeForest challenged the ruling through constitutional amparo proceedings, arguing that the labor court's interpretation violated the client's due process rights and improperly disregarded legally recognised identity documentation.
The Collegiate Court granted constitutional relief, ordered recognition of the attorney's legal standing and restored the client's right to present its defence.

comparisons.incremental_contribution: SCOTCH aporta una transformación normativa concreta bajo REPSE, revisión de estructura corporativa y laboral y auditoría de más de 80 proveedores, además de sostener la candidatura de José Alberto Díaz Méndez. Ramsa demuestra auditorías, terminaciones y capacitación, pero no aporta igual especificidad regulatoria ni una conexión individual equivalente.

development.positioning: Práctica employer-side para empleadores industriales, de infraestructura, tecnología, servicios y consumo, particularmente cuando la continuidad operativa depende de relaciones colectivas estables, integración de plantilla, cumplimiento laboral y de seguridad social, y gestión coordinada de controversias.
development.hero_rationale: El mandato de integración post-adquisición es el hero porque combina una transformación laboral específica y personalmente atribuida a Eduardo Garduño: armonización de documentación individual y colectiva, reglamentos, comisiones mixtas y políticas de gobierno laboral en seis estados para una plantilla superior a 5.000 empleados, además de 35 procedimientos laborales activos. Frente a la cartera industrial con exposición cercana a MXN280 millones, este mandato demuestra con mayor precisión una intervención organizacional definida, multijurisdiccional y de alcance colectivo.
development.target_rationale: Se preserva el objetivo primario suministrado de first-time recognition. La verificación de Chambers & Partners disponible no encontró una coincidencia exacta de la firma en la tabla examinada de Labour & Employment, Mexico; ello no confirma que la firma carezca de ranking global ni establece una posición actual. El objetivo secundario de “Move up multiple bands/tiers” no se utiliza porque no hay una posición actual verificada que permita describir una promoción.
development.principal_strength: La cartera demuestra una práctica employer-side integrada: integración post-adquisición en seis estados para más de 5.000 empleados; negociación colectiva y controversias de representatividad sindical; plataformas de litigación de aproximadamente 200 procedimientos activos; reestructuraciones bajo el régimen de servicios especializados; y gobierno laboral y de seguridad social para operaciones industriales y geográficamente dispersas.
development.filing_recommendation: Presentar una candidatura de reconocimiento inicial, articulada como práctica employer-side con evidencia de relaciones colectivas, integración de plantillas, reestructuraciones, litigación laboral, seguridad social y gobierno preventivo. No presentar el objetivo secundario de subida de bandas: no existe una posición actual de firma verificada desde la cual sostenerlo.
development.principal_vulnerability: No se suministró evidencia comparativa de mercado ni referencias de clientes, y no existe una posición actual verificada de firma o de los abogados en la práctica y alcance examinados. La atribución individual es sólida para Eduardo Garduño, Javier Atzin Vallejo y Jaime Bustamante. Para José Alberto Díaz Méndez, los rótulos fuente de “Lead Partner” deben mantenerse como atribución de responsabilidad en el asunto, sin presentarlo como socio, pues su rol confirmado para este periodo es Associate. La ausencia de research period y de algunos estados formales de asuntos es una advertencia de metadatos; conviene confirmar una vez que los mandatos seleccionados tuvieron actividad relevante en el periodo aplicable.

repair_feedback.message: Eliminar o sustituir por “categoría pendiente para socio” la nueva propuesta de Band 5 para Javier Atzin Vallejo. La fuente proponía “Associate to Watch”, categoría incompatible con su rol confirmado de Partner, pero la reparación inventó una banda específica sin evidencia comparativa externa. El estado not_found tampoco acredita una posición de mercado. La corrección debe conservar su candidatura como socio y explicar la incompatibilidad del objetivo original, sin predecir una banda.

Suggested ranking: Band 5 candidate

strategy.thesis: The selected confidential and publishable evidence supports an employer-side Labour & Employment submission centred on collective bargaining and union-representation disputes, workforce integration and restructurings, labor litigation portfolios, constitutional remedies, and labor/social-security governance for industrial and geographically dispersed workforces. SCHAEFFLER is the hero because it most clearly combines post-acquisition integration across six states, a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees and linked active proceedings. The submission objective is first-time recognition; no firm or individual Chambers ranking is established by the supplied verification, which records no exact scoped match rather than confirming any unranked status.

matters.rationale: Core and hero: this is the most complete source-backed combination of large-scale workforce integration, multi-state implementation, collective-labor harmonisation and linked contentious work.
matters.source_quote: The firm designed and implemented the labor integration strategy affecting facilities in Puebla, Estado de México, Guanajuato, Jalisco, Morelos and Chihuahua, standardising employment agreements, collective bargaining agreements, internal regulations, mixed commissions and labor governance policies for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees.
matters.legal_understanding: Post-acquisition labor integration following Schaeffler's global acquisition of Vitesco Technologies. The firm designed and implemented harmonised employment, collective-bargaining and governance documentation across facilities in six Mexican states for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees, while managing 35 active labor proceedings. The status field is recorded as N/A, but the narrative describes the project as currently underway; no completed transaction or litigation outcome should be inferred.

matters.source_quote: Through proactive dialogue and careful procedural management, the firm successfully prevented work stoppages and avoided escalation under the USMCA Rapid Response labor Mechanism, protecting both operational continuity and the client's long-term industrial stability.
matters.legal_understanding: Ongoing employer-side collective labor dispute over ownership of a collective bargaining agreement at a Querétaro manufacturing facility. The firm designed and implemented negotiation and litigation strategy in union-representation proceedings. The source states that work stoppages were prevented and escalation under the USMCA Rapid Response Labor Mechanism was avoided; these are source-reported results rather than independently verified findings.

editorial_development.c2:
DeForest respectfully seeks first-time recognition for its Labour & Employment practice in Mexico. The firm presents an employer-side practice that combines collective labour relations, workforce transformation, labour litigation, constitutional remedies, social-security work and preventive governance for industrial, infrastructure, technology, consumer-facing and regulated businesses.

Representative work includes a post-acquisition labour integration across six Mexican states for more than 5,000 employees, alongside 35 active labour proceedings; collective bargaining and union-representation mandates that have prevented work stoppages; a nationwide platform of approximately 200 active labour proceedings; and specialised-services restructurings involving employer substitutions, REPSE analysis and audits of more than 80 suppliers. The practice also handles employment investigations, labour and IMSS inspections, project-workforce structures and social-security litigation.

Eduardo Garduño, Javier Atzin Vallejo and Jaime Bustamante lead mandates across collective bargaining, industrial workforce governance, litigation and regulatory-risk management. José Alberto Díaz Méndez contributes to restructuring and specialised-services matters. Together, these mandates show a team supporting employers through the employment lifecycle, from preventive design and workforce integration to collective disputes and complex contentious matters.
editorial_development.b10:
DeForest’s Labour & Employment practice advises employers on workforce stability, collective labour relations, labour litigation, social security, compliance and workforce governance across Mexico. The team acts for industrial, infrastructure, technology, consumer-facing and regulated businesses where employment strategy is closely connected to operational continuity.

The practice combines contentious and non-contentious work. Its mandates include post-acquisition workforce integration across six Mexican states for more than 5,000 employees; collective bargaining and union-representativeness proceedings; nationwide litigation platforms involving hundreds of active matters; labour restructurings and employer-substitution processes; constitutional amparo proceedings; inspections and social-security matters; and specialised-services and REPSE projects.

The team’s work is particularly relevant to employers with manufacturing operations, geographically dispersed personnel, regulated workforces and sensitive union relationships. It designs employment documentation, collective bargaining frameworks, internal regulations, disciplinary procedures, compliance programmes and workforce-transition structures, while coordinating litigation and conciliation where disputes arise.

Eduardo Garduño leads employer-side mandates involving workforce integration, collective labour relations and labour-governance programmes. Javier Atzin Vallejo focuses on collective labour disputes, social security, infrastructure-related workforce structures and constitutional litigation. Jaime Bustamante advises on labour disputes, compliance, internal investigations and employment-risk management. José Alberto Díaz Méndez contributes to labour and social-security restructuring, REPSE analysis and administrative litigation, supported by a broader team working across contentious and advisory matters.

The practice’s identity is an integrated employer-side offering: collective relations, workforce transformation, litigation and preventive governance are managed as connected elements of operational continuity.

He leads the labour integration following an automotive supplier’s global acquisition, harmonising employment agreements, collective bargaining agreements, internal regulations, mixed commissions and labour-governance policies across six Mexican states for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees. He also leads an integrated labour-governance mandate for a major industrial employer, combining active proceedings with advice on employment agreements, workplace regulations, disciplinary procedures and corporate powers of attorney.

His collective-labour work includes leading negotiations for an automotive supplier facing an imminent strike risk, as well as workforce-transformation and collective-bargaining work across manufacturing facilities in Puebla, Veracruz and Tlaxcala. His practice further includes union-representativeness proceedings, geographically dispersed workforces and employment governance in regulated industrial environments.

candidates.submission_bio:
Javier Atzin Vallejo is a partner advising employers on collective labour relations, labour litigation, social security and workforce governance in industrial and infrastructure-intensive operations.

He leads a collective labour dispute concerning the ownership of a collective bargaining agreement at a manufacturing facility in Querétaro. The mandate combines negotiation and litigation strategy in union-representation proceedings; the work prevented work stoppages and avoided escalation under the USMCA Rapid Response Labor Mechanism. He also leads labour-governance work for major energy infrastructure projects, including project-specific employment structures, compliance programmes, dispute-prevention measures and workforce demobilisation.

His contentious work includes constitutional amparo proceedings that restored an employer’s right to present its defence after a labour court refused to recognise its attorney-in-fact. He also leads a wrongful-termination disputes mandate in which one principal claim was reduced from approximately MXN1.06 million to MXN20,000 through constitutional litigation, procedural strategy and settlement discussions.

comparisons.tradeoff: Securitas demuestra gestión de una plantilla descentralizada en seguridad privada. Cinemex aporta mayor escala litigiosa, una combinación más completa de litigación y prevención, y mejor apoyo a la candidatura de Eduardo Garduño y a la visibilidad de Erick Pérez.
comparisons.incremental_contribution: Cinemex aporta una plataforma nacional de aproximadamente 200 procedimientos activos, exposición superior a MXN60.5 millones, conciliaciones, reestructuraciones y participación atribuida a Erick Pérez. Securitas aporta más de 50 procedimientos y cobertura en cuatro ciudades, pero no iguala la escala ni la contribución individual al bench seleccionado.

comparisons.tradeoff: El mandato alternativo podría demostrar una disputa de gran escala, pero alteraría la identidad employer-side de la candidatura. Bonatti preserva coherencia con el posicionamiento seleccionado y respalda directamente a Javier Atzin Vallejo.
comparisons.incremental_contribution: Bonatti combina estructuras laborales de proyectos energéticos, más de 20 controversias, conciliación reportada, reducción aproximada del 80% de la exposición financiera potencial y prevención de huelga dentro de una narrativa employer-side. El asunto alternativo presenta una cuantía excepcional y mediación compleja, pero el cliente es expresamente un ex ejecutivo empleado.

comparisons.tradeoff: Ramsa ampliaría la evidencia preventiva de Jaime Bustamante; SCOTCH se mantiene porque añade una dimensión REPSE diferenciada y es el mandato más útil para demostrar la contribución de José Alberto Díaz Méndez.
comparisons.incremental_contribution: SCOTCH aporta una transformación normativa concreta bajo REPSE, revisión de estructura corporativa y laboral y auditoría de más de 80 proveedores, además de sostener la candidatura de José Alberto Díaz Méndez. Ramsa demuestra auditorías, terminaciones y capacitación, pero no aporta igual especificidad regulatoria ni una conexión individual equivalente.

editorial_development.positioning: Práctica employer-side para empleadores industriales, de infraestructura, tecnología, servicios y consumo, particularmente cuando la continuidad operativa depende de relaciones colectivas estables, integración de plantilla, cumplimiento laboral y de seguridad social, y gestión coordinada de controversias.
editorial_development.hero_rationale: El mandato de integración post-adquisición es el hero porque combina una transformación laboral específica y personalmente atribuida a Eduardo Garduño: armonización de documentación individual y colectiva, reglamentos, comisiones mixtas y políticas de gobierno laboral en seis estados para una plantilla superior a 5.000 empleados, además de 35 procedimientos laborales activos. Frente a la cartera industrial con exposición cercana a MXN280 millones, este mandato demuestra con mayor precisión una intervención organizacional definida, multijurisdiccional y de alcance colectivo.
editorial_development.target_rationale: Se preserva el objetivo primario suministrado de first-time recognition. La verificación de Chambers & Partners disponible no encontró una coincidencia exacta de la firma en la tabla examinada de Labour & Employment, Mexico; ello no confirma que la firma carezca de ranking global ni establece una posición actual. El objetivo secundario de “Move up multiple bands/tiers” no se utiliza porque no hay una posición actual verificada que permita describir una promoción.
editorial_development.principal_strength: La cartera demuestra una práctica employer-side integrada: integración post-adquisición en seis estados para más de 5.000 empleados; negociación colectiva y controversias de representatividad sindical; plataformas de litigación de aproximadamente 200 procedimientos activos; reestructuraciones bajo el régimen de servicios especializados; y gobierno laboral y de seguridad social para operaciones industriales y geográficamente dispersas.
editorial_development.filing_recommendation: Presentar una candidatura de reconocimiento inicial, articulada como práctica employer-side con evidencia de relaciones colectivas, integración de plantillas, reestructuraciones, litigación laboral, seguridad social y gobierno preventivo. No presentar el objetivo secundario de subida de bandas: no existe una posición actual de firma verificada desde la cual sostenerlo.
editorial_development.principal_vulnerability: No se suministró evidencia comparativa de mercado ni referencias de clientes, y no existe una posición actual verificada de firma o de los abogados en la práctica y alcance examinados. La atribución individual es sólida para Eduardo Garduño, Javier Atzin Vallejo y Jaime Bustamante. Para José Alberto Díaz Méndez, los rótulos fuente de “Lead Partner” deben mantenerse como atribución de responsabilidad en el asunto, sin presentarlo como socio, pues su rol confirmado para este periodo es Associate. La ausencia de research period y de algunos estados formales de asuntos es una advertencia de metadatos; conviene confirmar una vez que los mandatos seleccionados tuvieron actividad relevante en el periodo aplicable.

defects.message: Falta el periodo o una fecha opcional. Puedes completar este dato; su ausencia no impide construir ni entregar el documento.

acceptance.evidence: El documento conserva mandatos, roles, estados pendientes y conceptos monetarios sin mezclarlos. Por ejemplo, Cinemex distingue “USD553,278.59” de la exposición de “MXN60.5 million”; Bonatti separa el valor litigioso de aproximadamente USD252,000 de los valores de proyecto; y José Alberto Díaz Méndez aparece como Associate y “lead lawyer”, sin repetir la etiqueta fuente conflictiva de “Lead Partner”. No se presentan resultados pendientes como victorias.

Los 20 asuntos de la selección canónica aparecen en D/E y mantienen sus elementos decisivos: SCHAEFFLER conserva seis estados, más de 5,000 empleados, 35 procedimientos y el liderazgo de Eduardo Garduño; Brose conserva la prevención de paros y del escalamiento bajo el USMCA RRM; Volkswagen conserva la exposición cercana a MXN280 millones; y los demás asuntos retienen sus escalas, contribuciones, resultados o ausencia expresa de resultado.

Los clientes confidenciales se identifican únicamente en la sección E y en el Audit interno. B9, B10 y C2 describen esos mandatos mediante referencias anonimizadas como “a confidential automotive supplier” o por sus características sustantivas. La sección D contiene únicamente SCOTCH, cuyo estado confirmado es publishable. No se detectan nombres de asuntos confidenciales en las secciones públicas B9/B10/C2/D.

El Audit cubre a los ocho abogados con rango actual declarado o limitación de verificación, objetivo propuesto, fundamento, asuntos, rol personal, evidencia externa, brechas y acción. Distingue correctamente not_found de una condición global de Unranked; conserva Band 5 sólo como objetivo de Eduardo Garduño; elimina Associate to Watch para Javier Atzin Vallejo por ser socio confirmado; y desarrolla una candidatura Associate to Watch compatible con el cargo confirmado de José Alberto Díaz Méndez.

B9 desarrolla casos personalmente atribuidos para Eduardo Garduño, Javier Atzin Vallejo, Jaime Bustamante y José Alberto Díaz Méndez, vinculando a cada uno con mandatos, escalas y funciones concretas. Para Erick Pérez, Andrés Cabrera, Raymundo Carreño y Edgar Barreto, el texto evita inventar liderazgo y limita la descripción a la evidencia disponible.

C2 contiene el argumento desarrollado y respaldado para first-time recognition: integración post-adquisición en seis estados y más de 5,000 empleados, 35 procedimientos activos, prevención de paros, aproximadamente 200 procedimientos nacionales y restructuraciones REPSE con auditoría de más de 80 proveedores. No presenta el objetivo como ranking ya obtenido.

Submission, strategy y Audit comparten la misma cartera central de 20 asuntos y el mismo héroe, SCHAEFFLER. El Audit explica comparativamente SCHAEFFLER frente a Volkswagen y ofrece comparaciones fronterizas concretas: Cinemex frente a Securitas, Bonatti frente al asunto employee-side de Enerflex y SCOTCH frente a Ramsa. También justifica las exclusiones de Corrugados, Sirushi/Shirushi y AUNDE.

El Audit incluye veredicto y target, limitaciones de verificación, justificación comparativa del héroe, cartera ordenada, estrategia para todos los candidatos, reservas y exclusiones, y acciones previas al filing. Explica que el objetivo secundario de subida de bandas no procede sin una posición actual verificada y reconoce honestamente la ausencia de referencias y evidencia comparativa de mercado.

**Cartera recomendada — núcleo ordenado, con SCHAEFFLER como héroe**

1. **SCHAEFFLER — héroe.** Integración laboral post-adquisición en seis estados, para más de 5.000 empleados, con 35 procedimientos laborales activos; Eduardo Garduño lidera.
2. **Brose México.** Estrategia de negociación y litigio en una controversia de representatividad sindical; la fuente reporta prevención de paros y de escalamiento bajo el USMCA RRM; Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera.
3. **Volkswagen de México y Volkswagen Financial Services.** Cartera activa con exposición aproximada de MXN280 millones, combinada con documentación, reglamentos, disciplina y gobierno laboral; Eduardo Garduño lidera.
4. **Cinemex.** Plataforma nacional de aproximadamente 200 procedimientos activos, conciliaciones, restructuración y prevención para una fuerza laboral superior a 11.000 personas; Eduardo Garduño y Fernanda Priego figuran como líderes.
5. **GeNI de México.** Negociación colectiva ante riesgo inminente de huelga; la fuente reporta acuerdo renovado y continuidad productiva; Eduardo Garduño y Carlos Rivera figuran como líderes.
6. **Bonatti.** Estructuras laborales de ciclo completo para infraestructura energética, más de 20 controversias y prevención de una huelga reportada; Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera.
7. **Poliuretanos Summa Woodbridge.** Restructuración de aproximadamente ocho compañías, entidad de servicios especializados, sustituciones patronales y litigio de seguridad social pendiente; José Alberto Díaz Méndez figura como responsable del asunto y su cargo confirmado es Associate.
8. **Coats de México.** Transformación de plantilla en Puebla, Veracruz y Tlaxcala, con negociación colectiva y asuntos sindicales de exposición superior a MXN12,5 millones; Eduardo Garduño lidera.
9. **Recicla Ambiente.** Coordinación de estrategia laboral, negociación colectiva y relaciones sindicales para aproximadamente 700 empleados en seis localidades.
10. **Benteler.** Respuesta a controversia de representatividad sindical mediante litigio, estrategia colectiva y negociaciones con sindicatos competidores; Eduardo Garduño lidera.
11. **BADAK.** Defensa de reclamaciones por terminación; la fuente reporta reducción de una reclamación de aproximadamente MXN1,06 millones a MXN20.000, mientras continúan otros procedimientos; Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera.
12. **Nueva Empresa.** Amparo laboral que, según la fuente, obtuvo reconocimiento de la personería del apoderado y restituyó el derecho de defensa; Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera.
13. **Mextypsa.** Estructuración y desmovilización de plantilla para infraestructura, amparo y más de 20 controversias laborales en curso; Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera.
14. **Robert Bosch de México.** Documentación laboral, disciplina, asuntos sindicales, altas patronales y coordinación de seguridad social para una organización descrita con aproximadamente 17.000 empleados.

**Estrategia individual.** La limitación común es clara: para los ocho abogados, la verificación de Chambers para Labour & Employment, México, arroja *not found* en la tabla examinada. Ese resultado no confirma ausencia de ranking en otras prácticas o ediciones y no constituye reconocimiento individual. Las categorías siguientes son objetivos de candidatura, no rangos establecidos.

**Eduardo Garduño — presentar como candidato individual principal; objetivo Band 5.** Es socio confirmado y concentra la evidencia individual más sólida. Lidera el héroe SCHAEFFLER; el mandato integrado de Volkswagen; la transformación y negociación colectiva de Coats; y la negociación de GeNI ante riesgo de huelga. Esta combinación acredita liderazgo personalmente atribuido en integración post-adquisición, relaciones colectivas, litigación de escala y gobierno laboral industrial. Su objetivo Band 5 procede del objetivo suministrado y debe presentarse sólo como candidatura. Próximo paso: obtener referencias que validen liderazgo, servicio y criterio comercial.

**Javier Atzin Vallejo — presentar como segundo candidato socio; categoría pendiente.** Es socio confirmado. Lidera Brose, Bonatti, Nueva Empresa y BADAK, articulando disputas colectivas, prevención de paros, proyectos energéticos, amparo y defensa de reclamaciones laborales. El objetivo fuente de “Associate to Watch” es incompatible con su condición confirmada de socio y ha sido correctamente sustituido por una categoría pendiente para socio; no hay base externa para proponer una banda. Próximo paso: definir un objetivo individual compatible con socio, sustentado en referencias y evidencia externa disponible.

**Jaime Bustamante — desarrollar como candidato socio; categoría pendiente.** Es socio confirmado y aparece como líder en Tekia, Art Human y Grupo Radio Centro. Los asuntos atribuidos muestran litigación compleja con amparo pendiente, auditorías e inspecciones laborales y de seguridad social, y una investigación interna sensible. La evidencia respalda una narrativa diferenciada de gestión de riesgo laboral, pero aún no define una categoría individual concreta. Próximo paso: obtener un objetivo de categoría y referencias que acrediten su liderazgo en esos mandatos.

**José Alberto Díaz Méndez — presentar como candidato Associate to Watch.** Su cargo confirmado es Associate. La fuente le atribuye responsabilidad en SCOTCH, Grupo Solana y PSW: REPSE y auditoría de más de 80 proveedores; sustitución patronal; y restructuración multi-entidad con componente de seguridad social. También aparece como miembro nombrado en Volkswagen, Coats, Benteler y Bosch. Esta concentración respalda una candidatura de Associate to Watch, siempre describiéndolo como Associate y responsable de los trabajos, nunca como socio. Próximo paso: obtener referencias y detalles de ejecución individual —por ejemplo, estrategia, autoridad, negociación o dirección técnica— para reforzar la candidatura.

**Erick Pérez — desarrollar, no presentar como candidato individual formal.** Es Associate confirmado y aparece como miembro de equipo en Cinemex, Volkswagen y Benteler. La evidencia apoya visibilidad de bench en litigación nacional, gobierno industrial y controversias sindicales, pero no especifica su función jurídica individual. Próximo paso: documentar al menos dos mandatos con responsabilidad concreta en litigio, inspección o negociación colectiva.

**Andrés Cabrera — no presentar este ciclo.** Es Associate confirmado, pero ningún asunto seleccionado le atribuye un mandato o rol individual. Su perfil de litigación laboral es coherente con la práctica, aunque una biografía no sustituye asuntos personalmente atribuidos. Próximo paso: reunir al menos dos mandatos relevantes con responsabilidad, actividad y resultado claramente descritos.

Su experiencia histórica puede enriquecer una biografía, pero no acredita una candidatura actual. Próximo paso: incorporar trabajo reciente con rol específico en defensa, terminaciones o conciliación.

letter.executive_assessment:
**Veredicto ejecutivo — presentar para reconocimiento inicial.** La propuesta vigente sostiene una candidatura de primera inclusión en Labour & Employment, México, no una subida de bandas: la verificación disponible no encontró una coincidencia exacta de DeForest Abogados en la tabla examinada, lo que no acredita ausencia de ranking global ni una posición actual. Por ello, el objetivo secundario de “Move up multiple bands/tiers” queda correctamente descartado.

La principal fortaleza de la evidencia presentada es una práctica employer-side cohesionada que conecta relaciones colectivas, integración de plantillas, restructuraciones, litigación laboral, amparo, seguridad social y gobierno preventivo. La selección no se apoya únicamente en volumen: muestra intervenciones concretas en conflictos de representatividad sindical, negociación colectiva, transiciones de empleador, REPSE y plataformas de litigación para empleadores industriales, de infraestructura y de consumo.

El héroe debe seguir siendo **SCHAEFFLER**. Frente al mandato de Volkswagen, que aporta una exposición litigiosa mayor, SCHAEFFLER ofrece una demostración más precisa de transformación laboral: integración posterior a una adquisición, armonización de documentación individual y colectiva, reglamentos, comisiones mixtas y políticas de gobierno en seis estados para más de 5.000 empleados, junto con 35 procedimientos activos. Además, atribuye claramente el liderazgo a Eduardo Garduño.

La principal vulnerabilidad no es de práctica, sino de validación externa: no se suministran referencias de clientes ni evidencia comparativa de mercado, y la investigación de ranking no establece reconocimiento individual o institucional. Las afirmaciones de resultados se deben mantener como resultados reportados por las fuentes, sin transformarlas en validación independiente ni en previsiones de ranking.

Its representative work includes post-acquisition labour integration across six states for more than 5,000 employees; strategic collective bargaining and union-representation disputes in manufacturing and energy infrastructure; nationwide employment-litigation portfolios involving approximately 200 active proceedings; and multi-company restructurings involving specialised-services entities, employer substitutions and workforce transitions. editorial_previous_drafts.b10:
DeForest’s Labour & Employment practice advises employers on matters where workforce stability, regulatory compliance and operational continuity are closely connected. The team combines labour advisory, collective labour relations, employment litigation, social security, workplace compliance and workforce governance for domestic and multinational businesses operating throughout Mexico.

The practice is active in labour-intensive and regulated sectors, including automotive manufacturing, infrastructure, energy, logistics, technology, telecommunications, financial services and consumer-facing operations. Its work spans the employment lifecycle, from employment documentation, workplace regulations, labour policies and inspections to collective bargaining, union-representation disputes, workforce restructurings, REPSE compliance, employer substitutions, social security matters and litigation.

Representative work includes post-acquisition labour integration across six Mexican states for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees; collective bargaining and union-representation matters in which the team prevented threatened work stoppages; nationwide employment-litigation portfolios involving hundreds of active proceedings; and multi-company restructurings involving specialised-services entities, workforce transitions and social security litigation.

Eduardo Garduño leads complex workforce integration, collective labour and employment-litigation mandates. Javier Atzin Vallejo leads work involving industrial relations, social security, strategic infrastructure projects and constitutional employment litigation. Jaime Bustamante advises on workforce strategy, employment disputes, compliance and employment-risk management. José Alberto Díaz Méndez leads mandates involving REPSE, employer substitutions, labour restructuring and social security matters.

The team’s approach integrates contentious and preventive work: managing active disputes while strengthening the documentation, labour-governance and collective-relations frameworks that support employers’ ongoing operations.

matters.text:
DeForest acts for an engineering and infrastructure business on labour governance for major projects, with Javier Atzin Vallejo identified as Lead Partner. The work includes the Guadalajara Metro Line 4 Project, a USD 552 million development requiring project-based recruitment, documentation, workforce administration and eventual demobilisation, as well as litigation arising from a wind-farm project.

The team designed contractual and compliance architecture for the metro project and supervised workforce demobilisation to minimise post-project contingencies. In the wind-farm dispute, it successfully challenged an adverse labour judgment through constitutional proceedings, restoring the employer’s procedural rights and reopening the litigation. DeForest currently manages more than 20 labour disputes for the employer, representing aggregate exposure of approximately MXN 21.5 million.

DeForest advises an energy-infrastructure contractor on labour governance for major projects, including the Energía Mayakan Pipeline Expansion, valued at more than USD 2 billion, and the Cuxtal II expansion, valued at USD 2.5 billion. Javier Atzin Vallejo is identified as Lead Partner. The ongoing mandate includes workforce documentation, project-specific employment structures, compliance programmes, dispute-prevention strategies and workforce demobilisation.

Alongside this preventive work, the team managed more than 20 labour disputes arising during project execution, resolving the overwhelming majority through conciliation and reducing potential financial exposure by approximately 80%. DeForest also prevented an imminent strike that threatened to halt operations linked to strategic energy infrastructure.

Following a global acquisition, DeForest was appointed to lead the post-acquisition labour integration of an automotive supplier’s Mexican manufacturing operations. Eduardo Garduño is identified as Lead Partner. The mandate covered facilities in Puebla, Estado de México, Guanajuato, Jalisco, Morelos and Chihuahua and required harmonisation of employment structures while operations continued.

The team designed and implemented a labour integration strategy for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees, standardising employment agreements, collective bargaining agreements, internal regulations, mixed commissions and labour-governance policies. In parallel, DeForest manages 35 active labour proceedings involving suppliers and former employees, aligning litigation strategy with the employer’s unified post-acquisition governance model.

DeForest advises an automotive supplier in an ongoing collective bargaining matter arising from a deteriorating union relationship and an imminent strike risk. Eduardo Garduño and Carlos Rivera are identified as Lead Partners. The threatened disruption had the potential to affect production across multiple automotive supply chains.

The firm led collective bargaining negotiations, rebuilding dialogue between management and union representatives and designing a renewed agreement that balanced operational efficiency with employee expectations. The negotiations prevented the strike and introduced process improvements and operational efficiencies while uninterrupted production was preserved.

DeForest represents a private-sector employer in two ongoing wrongful-termination proceedings. Javier Atzin Vallejo is identified as Lead Partner. The matters arose after a labour court refused to recognise the company’s attorney-in-fact, disregarded the employer’s defence and issued an adverse ruling despite notarial documentation concerning the attorney’s legal identity.

The team challenged the ruling through constitutional amparo proceedings, arguing that the court’s approach violated due process and improperly disregarded legally recognised identity documentation. The Collegiate Court granted constitutional relief, ordered recognition of the attorney’s standing and restored the employer’s right to present its defence. The source describes financial exposure of approximately MXN 3 million.

DeForest represents a manufacturing employer in an ongoing collective labour dispute concerning ownership of a collective bargaining agreement at a facility in Querétaro. Javier Atzin Vallejo is identified as Lead Partner. The matter arose amid union-representation challenges under Mexico’s changing collective labour framework, with direct business-continuity implications for the operation.

The team designed and implemented the employer’s negotiation and litigation strategy, combining proactive dialogue with procedural management in the representation proceedings. DeForest prevented work stoppages and avoided escalation under the USMCA Rapid Response Labor Mechanism while preserving uninterrupted operations.

DeForest advises a private-security employer on employment litigation and preventive workforce governance as the business expands across Puebla, Mexico City, Torreón and Veracruz. Eduardo Garduño is identified as Lead Partner, with Maximiliano Hernández and Erick Pérez listed as team members. The employer operates a dispersed workforce and faces ongoing employment and regulatory exposure.

The firm manages more than 50 labour proceedings with aggregate exposure approaching MXN 10 million. Alongside the litigation portfolio, DeForest advises on documentation, employment governance and risk mitigation, applying a coordinated strategy across the employer’s multi-jurisdictional operations.

DeForest acts for an engineering and technology business on an ongoing portfolio of legacy employment litigation involving potential exposure approaching MXN 16 million. Jaime Bustamante is identified as Lead Partner. The mandate includes negotiations relating to two adverse labour judgments valued at approximately MXN 6.5 million and a constitutional amparo challenging the reasoning underlying one of the labour decisions.

The firm designed a coordinated strategy combining litigation, constitutional review and commercial negotiation to contain overall financial risk. The constitutional amparo remains ongoing.

DeForest represents a technology consultancy in several employment disputes involving wrongful-termination claims with aggregate exposure exceeding MXN 1.5 million. Javier Atzin Vallejo is identified as Lead Partner. One principal claim had escalated to approximately MXN 1.06 million when constitutional relief became available.

The team combined constitutional litigation, procedural strategy and commercial negotiation. Through sequencing of legal actions and settlement discussions, DeForest reduced the principal claim from approximately MXN 1.06 million to MXN 20,000, representing a reduction of approximately 98%, while continuing to manage the remaining proceedings.

DeForest continues to advise a major industrial employer and its financial-services affiliate on labour governance for their Mexican operations. Eduardo Garduño is identified as Lead Partner, with José Alberto Díaz, Erick Pérez, Ana Ruiz and Ariam Barrientos listed as team members. The ongoing mandate combines contentious and preventive employment work for operations in Puebla.

The firm manages active labour proceedings involving aggregate exposure approaching MXN 280 million. It also advises on employment agreements, internal workplace regulations, disciplinary procedures, corporate powers of attorney and broader workforce-governance initiatives, integrating dispute management with preventive labour strategy.

DeForest advises an industrial employer with approximately 17,000 people across multiple business divisions on employment and labour governance. Javier Atzin Vallejo is identified as Lead Partner, and José Alberto Díaz is listed as a team member. The ongoing mandate addresses governance for a large industrial workforce.

The team advises on employment documentation, disciplinary procedures, labour-governance policies and union-related matters. It also leads employer-registration processes for a group company and coordinates social security structures across the organisation.

DeForest advises a manufacturer on an ongoing workforce transformation affecting facilities in Puebla, Veracruz and Tlaxcala. Eduardo Garduño is identified as Lead Partner, with José Alberto Díaz and Maximiliano Hernández listed as team members. The mandate combines redesign of the employment framework with sensitive collective labour issues relevant to manufacturing continuity.

The firm developed the employer’s labour architecture, including employment agreements, labour policies, collective bargaining documentation and workforce-governance protocols. It also negotiated union-related matters involving exposure exceeding MXN 12.5 million and led collective bargaining discussions that enabled the employer to preserve operational stability during the restructuring.

DeForest advises an industrial employer on the design of its labour-governance framework and on union-representativeness proceedings. Eduardo Garduño is identified as Lead Partner, with Ana Ruíz listed as a team member. The mandate combines preventive employment structures with collective labour representation in Mexico’s post-reform environment.

The firm designed employment documentation, labour policies and a collective bargaining framework, while leading union-representativeness proceedings requiring procedural strategy and continuing engagement with labour authorities.

DeForest represents an automotive supplier in a union-representativeness dispute affecting a manufacturing facility in Puebla. Eduardo Garduño is identified as Lead Partner, with José Alberto Díaz, Erick Pérez and Ariam Barrientos listed as team members. The matter concerns a collective labour dispute capable of disrupting operations.

The firm assumed responsibility for the employer’s strategic response, combining litigation, collective bargaining strategy and continuing negotiations with competing unions. Alongside the representation proceedings, the team is implementing employment agreements, internal labour policies and collective bargaining documentation to reinforce the employer’s labour-governance platform.

DeForest acts for a nationwide cinema operator with more than 11,000 employees on an ongoing employment-litigation and labour-governance mandate. Eduardo Garduño and Fernanda Priego are identified as Lead Partners, with Erick Pérez and Ariam Barrientos listed as team members.

The firm coordinates a nationwide litigation platform comprising approximately 200 active labour proceedings with aggregate exposure exceeding MXN 60.5 million. Its work includes conciliation proceedings, workforce restructurings, employment documentation and preventive governance measures intended to reduce future labour contingencies across the employer’s multi-jurisdictional workforce.

DeForest advises an employer operating approximately 700 employees across multiple Mexican states on labour governance and collective labour strategy. Eduardo Garduño is identified as Lead Partner. The workforce is geographically dispersed and the mandate involves negotiations with multiple unions.

The team advises on labour, collective bargaining and union negotiations in Puebla, Querétaro, Silao, Aguascalientes, Ramos Arizpe and Apodaca. It coordinates employment strategy across these jurisdictions while addressing local operational requirements and different union relationships.

DeForest advised SCOTCH on restructuring its corporate and labour framework following the introduction of Mexico’s specialised-services regime. José Alberto Díaz Méndez is identified as Lead Partner. The multidisciplinary mandate required alignment of the business model with the evolving outsourcing and REPSE framework.

Working across its corporate and labour practices, DeForest reviewed the client’s corporate structure, specialised-services model, bylaws and REPSE registration. The team also audited more than 80 suppliers to determine the appropriate regulatory treatment of specialised-services agreements.

DeForest advised a diversified automotive and real estate group employing more than 1,200 people on an employer-substitution process affecting its workforce structure. José Alberto Díaz Méndez is identified as Lead Partner. The project required coordination with labour and regulatory authorities after the group’s employer registration had been cancelled.

The team designed and executed the legal strategy to reactivate the employer registration, enabling the employer-substitution process to proceed without disrupting operations. DeForest coordinated the labour transition and addressed compliance with the applicable employment framework while preserving workforce stability during the restructuring.

José Alberto Díaz Méndez is identified as Lead Partner for DeForest’s labour restructuring mandate for a manufacturing group. The project affects approximately eight companies operating across multiple Mexican states and involves separation of business functions, redesign of the group’s employment model and development of a specialised-services platform under Mexico’s post-outsourcing framework.

DeForest developed the legal strategy for creation of a specialised-services entity, employer-substitution processes, redesign of corporate purposes and a workforce transition across the operating companies. The firm also represents the employer in social security litigation before the Federal Court of Administrative Justice challenging tax assessments relating to two manufacturing facilities.

The confirmed matter value is USD 1,144,523.00; the separate MXN figures described in the narrative concern project-specific exposures.

The team designed contractual and compliance architecture for the metro project and supervised workforce demobilisation to minimise post-project contingencies. In the wind-farm dispute, it successfully challenged an adverse labour judgment through constitutional proceedings, restoring the client’s procedural rights and reopening the litigation. DeForest currently manages more than 20 labour disputes for the client, representing aggregate exposure of approximately MXN 21.5 million.

DeForest advises Bonatti on labour governance for major energy-infrastructure projects, including the Energía Mayakan Pipeline Expansion, valued at more than USD 2 billion, and the Cuxtal II expansion, valued at USD 2.5 billion. Javier Atzin Vallejo is identified as Lead Partner. The ongoing mandate covers workforce documentation, project-specific employment structures, compliance programmes, dispute-prevention strategies and workforce demobilisation.

The team managed more than 20 labour disputes arising during project execution, resolving the overwhelming majority through conciliation and reducing potential financial exposure by approximately 80%. DeForest also prevented an imminent strike that threatened to halt operations linked to strategic energy infrastructure.

Following a global acquisition, DeForest was appointed to lead the post-acquisition labour integration of an automotive supplier’s Mexican manufacturing operations. Eduardo Garduño is identified as Lead Partner. The mandate covers facilities in Puebla, Estado de México, Guanajuato, Jalisco, Morelos and Chihuahua.

The team designed and implemented the labour integration strategy for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees, standardising employment agreements, collective bargaining agreements, internal regulations, mixed commissions and labour-governance policies. In parallel, DeForest manages 35 active labour proceedings involving suppliers and former employees, aligning litigation strategy with the client’s unified post-acquisition governance model.

DeForest advises GeNI de México, an automotive supplier, in an ongoing collective bargaining matter arising from a deteriorating union relationship and an imminent strike risk. Eduardo Garduño and Carlos Rivera are identified as Lead Partners. The threatened disruption had the potential to affect production across multiple automotive supply chains.

The firm led collective bargaining negotiations, rebuilding dialogue between management and union representatives and designing a renewed agreement that balanced operational efficiency with employee expectations. The negotiations prevented the strike and introduced process improvements and operational efficiencies while uninterrupted production was preserved.

DeForest represents Nueva Empresa, S.C. in two ongoing wrongful-termination proceedings. Javier Atzin Vallejo is identified as Lead Partner. The matters arose after a labour court refused to recognise the company’s attorney-in-fact, disregarded the employer’s defence and issued an adverse ruling despite notarial documentation concerning the attorney’s legal identity.

The team challenged the ruling through constitutional amparo proceedings, arguing that the court’s approach violated due process and improperly disregarded legally recognised identity documentation. The Collegiate Court granted constitutional relief, ordered recognition of the attorney’s standing and restored the employer’s right to present its defence. The confirmed matter value is approximately USD 171,494.21; the narrative separately describes financial exposure of approximately MXN 3 million.

DeForest represents Brose México in an ongoing collective labour dispute concerning ownership of a collective bargaining agreement at a manufacturing facility in Querétaro. Javier Atzin Vallejo is identified as Lead Partner. The matter arose amid union-representation challenges under Mexico’s evolving collective labour framework.

The team designed and implemented the client’s negotiation and litigation strategy, combining proactive dialogue with procedural management in the representation proceedings. DeForest prevented work stoppages and avoided escalation under the USMCA Rapid Response Labor Mechanism while preserving uninterrupted operations.

DeForest acts for Empresa Tekia on an ongoing portfolio of legacy employment litigation involving potential exposure approaching MXN 16 million. Jaime Bustamante is identified as Lead Partner. The mandate includes negotiations relating to two adverse labour judgments valued at approximately MXN 6.5 million and a constitutional amparo challenging the reasoning underlying one of the labour decisions.

The firm designed a coordinated strategy combining litigation, constitutional review and commercial negotiation to contain overall financial risk. The constitutional amparo remains ongoing.

DeForest represents BADAK in several employment disputes involving wrongful-termination claims with aggregate exposure exceeding MXN 1.5 million. Javier Atzin Vallejo is identified as Lead Partner. One principal claim had escalated to approximately MXN 1.06 million when constitutional relief became available.

The team combined constitutional litigation, procedural strategy and commercial negotiation. Through sequencing of legal actions and settlement discussions, DeForest reduced the principal claim from approximately MXN 1.06 million to MXN 20,000, representing a reduction of approximately 98%, while continuing to manage the remaining proceedings.

DeForest continues to advise Volkswagen de México and Volkswagen Financial Services on labour governance for their Mexican operations. Eduardo Garduño is identified as Lead Partner, with José Alberto Díaz, Erick Pérez, Ana Ruiz and Ariam Barrientos listed as team members. The ongoing mandate combines contentious and preventive employment work for operations in Puebla.

The firm manages active labour proceedings involving aggregate exposure approaching MXN 280 million. It also advises on employment agreements, internal workplace regulations, disciplinary procedures, corporate powers of attorney and broader workforce-governance initiatives, integrating dispute management with preventive labour strategy.

DeForest advises Robert Bosch de México, which employs approximately 17,000 people across multiple business divisions, on employment and labour governance. Javier Atzin Vallejo is identified as Lead Partner, and José Alberto Díaz is listed as a team member. The ongoing mandate addresses governance for a large industrial workforce.

The team advises on employment documentation, disciplinary procedures, labour-governance policies and union-related matters. It also leads employer-registration processes for Bosch Rexroth and coordinates social security structures across the organisation.

DeForest advises Coats de México on an ongoing workforce transformation affecting manufacturing facilities in Puebla, Veracruz and Tlaxcala. Eduardo Garduño is identified as Lead Partner, with José Alberto Díaz and Maximiliano Hernández listed as team members. The mandate combines redesign of the employment framework with sensitive collective labour issues relevant to manufacturing continuity.

The firm developed the client’s labour architecture, including employment agreements, labour policies, collective bargaining documentation and workforce-governance protocols. It also negotiated union-related matters involving exposure exceeding MXN 12.5 million and led collective bargaining discussions that enabled the client to preserve operational stability during the restructuring.

DeForest advises REGSA on the design of its labour-governance framework and on union-representativeness proceedings. Eduardo Garduño is identified as Lead Partner, with Ana Ruíz listed as a team member. The mandate combines preventive employment structures with collective labour representation in Mexico’s post-reform environment.

The firm designed employment documentation, labour policies and a collective bargaining framework, while leading union-representativeness proceedings requiring procedural strategy and continuing engagement with labour authorities.

DeForest represents Benteler in a union-representativeness dispute affecting a manufacturing facility in Puebla. Eduardo Garduño is identified as Lead Partner, with José Alberto Díaz, Erick Pérez and Ariam Barrientos listed as team members. The matter concerns a collective labour dispute capable of disrupting operations.

The firm assumed responsibility for the employer’s strategic response, combining litigation, collective bargaining strategy and continuing negotiations with competing unions. Alongside the representation proceedings, the team is implementing employment agreements, internal labour policies and collective bargaining documentation to reinforce the employer’s labour-governance platform.

DeForest acts for Cinemex, a nationwide cinema operator with more than 11,000 employees, on an ongoing employment-litigation and labour-governance mandate. Eduardo Garduño and Fernanda Priego are identified as Lead Partners, with Erick Pérez and Ariam Barrientos listed as team members.

The firm coordinates a nationwide litigation platform comprising approximately 200 active labour proceedings with aggregate exposure exceeding MXN 60.5 million. Its work includes conciliation proceedings, workforce restructurings, employment documentation and preventive governance measures designed to reduce future labour contingencies across the employer’s multi-jurisdictional workforce.

DeForest advises Recicla Ambiente, a company operating approximately 700 employees across multiple Mexican states, on labour governance and collective labour strategy. Eduardo Garduño is identified as Lead Partner. The workforce is geographically dispersed and the mandate involves negotiations with multiple unions.

The team advises on labour, collective bargaining and union negotiations in Puebla, Querétaro, Silao, Aguascalientes, Ramos Arizpe and Apodaca. It coordinates employment strategy across these jurisdictions while addressing local operational requirements and different union relationships.

DeForest advised SCOTCH on restructuring its corporate and labour framework following the introduction of Mexico’s specialised-services regime. José Alberto Díaz Méndez, an Associate, has documented responsibility on the matter. The multidisciplinary mandate required alignment of the business model with the evolving outsourcing and REPSE framework.

Working across its corporate and labour practices, DeForest reviewed the client’s corporate structure, specialised-services model, bylaws and REPSE registration. The team also audited more than 80 suppliers to determine the appropriate regulatory treatment of specialised-services agreements.

DeForest advised Grupo Solana, a diversified automotive and real estate group employing more than 1,200 people, on an employer-substitution process affecting its workforce structure. José Alberto Díaz Méndez, an Associate, has documented responsibility on the matter. The project required coordination with labour and regulatory authorities after the group’s employer registration had been cancelled.

The team designed and executed the legal strategy to reactivate the employer registration, enabling the employer-substitution process to proceed without disrupting operations. DeForest coordinated the labour transition and addressed compliance with the applicable employment framework while preserving workforce stability during the restructuring.

DeForest advises Poliuretanos Summa Woodbridge on a restructuring affecting approximately eight companies operating across multiple Mexican states. José Alberto Díaz Méndez, an Associate, has documented responsibility on the mandate. The project involves separation of business functions, redesign of the group’s employment model and development of a specialised-services platform under Mexico’s post-outsourcing framework.

The team developed the legal strategy for creation of a specialised-services entity, employer-substitution processes, redesign of corporate purposes and a workforce transition across the operating companies. In parallel, DeForest represents the client in social security litigation before the Federal Court of Administrative Justice challenging tax assessments relating to two manufacturing facilities.
